One villa in each city. The whole family, under one roof, twice over.

Flights in and out are yours to book — but once we land, everything is shared: the villas, the Bangkok–Phuket leg, the transfers, and six nights of celebrating Rosettus in style.

Getting there, and back

Travel & logistics

Flying in — Dec 28

International flights are booked individually — whatever works for your budget and airline. Our target is to land in Bangkok by 3:00 PM so the group can spend that first afternoon together. From the airport to the villa is on you for this leg — Grab or a metered taxi are the easiest options.

Bangkok → Phuket — Dec 31

This leg is booked individually — the organizing team will recommend a flight, but each person is responsible for purchasing their own. The airport transfer on arrival in Phuket is a group arrangement, covered by the activity fee. Nothing to book for that part.

Flying home — Jan 3

Departure flights are individual again. A recommended earliest departure time will be added here once checkout logistics are confirmed.

Good to know

Confirm your visa requirement before booking — it varies by passport, so check your own country's Thai embassy site. Domestic Thai flights, like our Dec 31 leg, often have tighter luggage weight limits than international ones.

On the ground

Hop in — this is how we move

Tuk-tuks, neon signs, and streets that never quite go quiet — this is the Bangkok in between our plans, the part you catch out of the corner of your eye on the way to dinner. Loud, a little chaotic, completely unforgettable.

Where we're staying

Two villas, one big glorious family reunion

Forget separate hotel rooms — we're taking over one villa in Bangkok and one in Phuket, the whole crew under one roof in each city. Morning coffee with everyone who matters, a pool to fall into after a long day of temples or islands, and zero reason to say goodnight before you're ready to.

The full details, if you're the type who likes to know exactly where you're sleeping.

Bangkok Villa

Dec 28 – Dec 31 · 3 nights
~$394 per person

11 bedrooms · 12 bathrooms · sleeps up to 28

Three private villas — S3, S5, and S6 — sharing one tropical courtyard and a pool right outside the door, tucked into a quiet corner of Sukhumvit. Every bedroom gets its own ensuite bathroom, the second-floor master has a walk-in closet and soaring ceilings over the living room below, and the third-floor rooms open onto a terrace looking out over the city. Minutes from Ekamai BTS, rooftop bars, and some of Bangkok's best restaurants — big enough that fifteen of us will barely notice each other unless we want to.

Phuket Villa

Dec 31 – Jan 3 · 3 nights
~$343 per person

7 bedrooms · 5.5 bathrooms · sleeps up to 16+

A six-floor hillside villa above Patong with a Guest Favorite rating and 700 square meters to spread out in. The fifth floor is the showstopper — a private pool looking straight out over Patong Bay, with a rooftop above it for sunset views. Two master suites with king beds and ensuites, a family room with two kings and its own pool access, an elevator for anyone who'd rather skip the stairs, and a wraparound terrace built for exactly the kind of group dinners we're planning.

Currency & cash

Thai Baht. As of late 2026, roughly 1 USD ≈ 33 THB — check a live rate closer to the trip. Cards work almost everywhere; bring $150–250 in cash for markets, tuk-tuks, and street food. ATMs in Thailand generally beat airport exchange counters.

Tipping

~10% at restaurants without a service charge · 20–50 THB for hotel staff/porters · ~100–200 THB per person, per day for guides · 100–200 THB for spa services · rounding up is enough for taxis.

Daily budget

Street food, $2–5 · casual restaurant, $10–15 · a nicer dinner, $25–40+. Plan for roughly $40–60 a day on free days.

Before you go

Packing & weather

Late December is Thailand's cool, dry season — the most pleasant time of year to visit. Bangkok runs 75–89°F with low humidity; Phuket sits in the low-to-mid 80s, with calm seas and little rain.

Pack this

  • Light, breathable clothing, plus one layer for air conditioning
  • A scarf or cover-up for temples — shoulders and knees
  • Comfortable shoes for temples and markets
  • Swimwear and reef-safe sunscreen for Phuket
  • A Type A/C/O adapter
  • A reusable water bottle

Good to know

  • Stick to bottled or filtered water
  • Passports valid 6 months beyond our travel dates
  • Check your own country's visa requirement before booking
  • Travel insurance is recommended for the group

Questions

Frequently asked

Where are we staying?

One villa in Bangkok, one villa in Phuket — the whole group together in each, not separate hotel rooms.

How do we get from Bangkok to Phuket, and the airport to the villa?

The Dec 31 flight is booked individually — the organizing team will recommend a flight, but you'll purchase your own. The Phuket airport transfer on arrival is coordinated as a group and covered by the activity fee — nothing for you to arrange there.

What's the weather really going to be like?

Cool and dry — Bangkok around 75–89°F with low humidity; Phuket similarly warm, low-to-mid 80s, calm seas, minimal rain.

Do I need a visa?

It depends on citizenship. Many nationalities, including U.S. passport holders, can currently enter Thailand visa-free for short stays — but confirm with your own country's Thai embassy closer to departure, since rules change.

What currency should I bring, and can I use cards?

Thai Baht — roughly 33 THB per USD as of late 2026. Cards cover hotels, malls, and most restaurants; bring some cash for markets and street food.

Is the water safe to drink?

Stick to bottled or filtered water. Ice at hotels and reputable restaurants is generally fine.

What if I have dietary restrictions?

Let the organizer know ahead of the group dinners so restaurants can be given notice.

What's the dress code for the birthday dinners?

To be confirmed once the venues are locked in — check back here.

Who do I contact in an emergency?
